route: Brescia → Tirano → Bernina Pass → St. Moritz → Tirano → Brescia
intro:
Today was one of those days that started with a little adventure and turned into something truly spectacular.

I left Brescia early this morning, heading north toward Tirano, where I would board the Bernina Express for the journey into Switzerland. I knew I had a 10:00 a.m. train to catch, so timing was important.

One of the challenges of driving through Europe has been trying to follow the on-screen GPS. It's not always the easiest thing to do, especially when cell service is delayed and the directions don't quite keep up with where you are. Before you know it, you've missed a turn or taken the wrong road.

And that's exactly what happened this morning.

But this particular wrong turn turned into something wonderful.

Instead of following my intended route, I found myself driving right alongside Lake Iseo. And when I say alongside the lake, I mean it almost felt as though I was driving directly on the water!

The lake was right there beside me, with the mountains rising around it. It was such a beautiful and unexpected experience. What could have been just another frustrating navigation mistake became one of those moments I know I'll remember for a long time.

Sometimes the wrong turn turns out to be the right one.

But the morning still had another surprise waiting for me.

As I approached one of the tunnels, traffic suddenly came to a stop. At first, I wasn't sure what was happening. Then I noticed the Italian fire department ahead. They stopped traffic so their vehicles could get through, and eventually we began moving slowly through the tunnel.

What made this particularly interesting was watching the firefighters inspecting the tunnel, shining their flashlights on different sections as we drove through.

I couldn't help wondering, "Is this thing safe? Is it going to collapse?"

Not exactly the kind of thought you want going through your mind while driving through a mountain tunnel!

The delay cost me several valuable minutes, and suddenly my comfortable arrival time in Tirano wasn't looking quite so comfortable anymore.

By the time I reached Tirano, I was cutting it extremely close.

After parking, I had to speed-walk and even run a little to reach the train. And I mean I barely made it. As soon as I stepped aboard, the train started moving!

Talk about timing!

After all that, I could finally settle into my seat and enjoy what I had come all this way to experience.

And what an experience it was.

As the Bernina Express began climbing through the Swiss Alps, the scenery became increasingly spectacular. But my first real “wow” moment came when we reached Lago di Poschiavo.

There it was, this beautiful lake nestled between steep, forested mountains, with the railway winding along its edge. Looking out from the train, watching the lake and mountains unfold together, I was simply amazed. It was one of those views that makes you realize just how extraordinary this journey really is.

And somehow, the scenery only kept getting better.

As we climbed higher toward the Bernina Pass, the landscape changed dramatically. The mountains became more rugged, and eventually we reached Lago Bianco, surrounded by magnificent alpine scenery.

The beauty alone would have made this moment unforgettable. The mountains, the lake, and the train winding through this incredible landscape were simply breathtaking.

But then came something I hadn’t expected to learn.

This area sits along a continental watershed. Water on one side flows toward the Adriatic Sea, while water on the other side eventually reaches the Black Sea!

That absolutely blew my mind! 🤯

Here I was, riding a train high through the Swiss Alps, surrounded by breathtaking mountains and lakes, discovering that water from this same mountain region could travel in completely opposite directions and eventually reach two different seas.

The scenery was incredible, but understanding that made it even more remarkable.

Eventually, the train arrived in St. Moritz, the famous Swiss alpine resort town.

Rather than spending my time exploring luxury shops, I wanted to experience the town itself and enjoy the scenery. After the excitement of the morning, it was nice to have some time to explore at a more relaxed pace.

For lunch, I stopped at Hauser, where I decided to try something local: pizokels, a traditional specialty from the Graubünden region of Switzerland.

It seemed only fitting to have a regional dish while visiting this part of the country.

And, of course, there was room for dessert!

I finished lunch with homemade profiteroles served with chocolate sauce and a cappuccino. A wonderful way to enjoy a little time in St. Moritz before heading back to the station.

The return journey gave me another opportunity to appreciate the extraordinary scenery of the Bernina railway. Having already experienced the excitement of the climb, I could reflect on everything I had seen throughout the day.

The mountains, the lakes, the dramatic changes in elevation, and the engineering required to build a railway through this landscape all made the journey remarkable.

What stays with me most, though, is how the day unfolded.

It began with an early morning drive through beautiful mountain scenery, an unexpected tunnel inspection, and a frantic dash to catch a train that literally started moving the moment I boarded.

Then came the beauty of Lago di Poschiavo, my first real “wow” moment of the journey, followed by the even more remarkable experience of Lago Bianco and learning about the watersheds that lead toward two different seas.

Sometimes the most memorable travel experiences aren’t just about seeing something beautiful. They’re about discovering something you never knew before.

And today gave me plenty of both.

It had been a remarkable experience, and one I was very glad I had included in this journey.

But the day wasn’t over.

By the time I returned to Tirano, evening was approaching, and I still had the drive back to Brescia ahead of me.

And this is where the name of my trip became especially appropriate.

The Long Way Around.

After a full day of driving, rushing to catch a train, exploring St. Moritz, and traveling across the Alps, I was tired.

And now it was dark.

I had already experienced plenty of narrow, single-lane roads and switchbacks on the way to Tirano that morning. I certainly didn’t want to repeat that experience at night, especially on unfamiliar mountain roads without streetlights.

There’s something particularly uncomfortable about driving the beast down a narrow road in complete darkness, not knowing whether another car might come around the next bend and leave us trying to squeeze past one another.

During the day, those roads are stressful enough. At night, when you’re tired and can’t see what’s coming, it’s an entirely different experience.

So I made the decision to take the longer route back, sticking to larger, more comfortable roads rather than risking another series of narrow mountain roads.

I was tired, and yes, a little scared of what those unlit roads might bring. I didn’t need another white-knuckle adventure. I just wanted to get back to Brescia safely.

And so, once again, I was literally taking the long way around.

It’s funny how the name of this trip continues to take on different meanings.

This morning, a wrong turn led me alongside Lake Iseo and gave me a memory I never expected.

Later, the Bernina Express carried me through some of the most spectacular scenery I’ve seen, past beautiful Alpine lakes and a watershed that sends water toward two different seas.

And tonight, taking the long way around simply meant choosing a road where I could feel more comfortable getting back to my hotel.

Not every detour has to lead to something spectacular.

Sometimes the best route is simply the one that gets you home safely.

But that’s all part of the adventure.

And what a day it has been.
